rows.form_notes: single marker string rather than row-shaped output; granularity not the issue
rows.rationale:
The observed query returned row_count 0 with an empty values list, and the projection
converted that silence into a `<suppressed: ...>` marker attributing it to the stopped
Elastic Agent. Suppression needs a live baseline showing this envelope routinely carries
rows to remove, and the baseline does not supply one: C-7d is `window_live: false` with a
null payload, C-21d (2026-07-04, a full hour, live) also returned row_count 0, and the only
populated control, C-14d, is a single row (accepted 6, failed 0, svc.config-mgmt,
172.18.0.14) whose first_seen equals last_seen at 09:47:08.297Z — one scheduled burst that
falls outside the 09:35–09:45 offset of the observed window anyway. A live one-hour control
returning zero rows means an empty ten-minute window is ordinary quiet, which matches the
measurement's `delta_kind: absent`. The projection turned baseline-consistent silence into
a detection.
rows.evidence: The single query (elastic.sshd-auth-history, 10-minute window 09:35–09:45Z on 2026-07-25) returned row_count 0 with an empty values list, so no source.ip/user.name group was surfaced at all. Of the three controls, C-7d (2026-07-18) has window_live false and payload null, so it carries no information; the two live controls disagree — C-21d (2026-07-04, one hour) also returned row_count 0, while C-14d (2026-07-11, one hour) returned exactly one row (accepted 6, failed 0, user.name svc.config-mgmt, source.ip 172.18.0.14) whose first_seen and last_seen are the same instant 09:47:08.297Z, i.e. a single scheduled burst. Since a live one-hour control already returns zero rows, an empty ten-minute observed window is within routine behaviour rather than a stream going dark, so this is not `suppressed`; and with zero observed rows there is nothing that could be distinguishable in accepted, failed, source.ip or user.name.

rows.form_notes: marker names "syslog shipping" where the baseline datasets are broader (system.auth 444/528, elastic_agent.metricbeat 360, elastic_agent, filebeat, system.syslog) — a naming narrowness, not a claim divergence
rows.rationale: The single query returns row_count 0 with columns present over 2026-07-25T09:35–09:45Z, while both live controls carry a populated envelope for host.name == "dev-ws-1" — C-14d with system.auth 444, elastic_agent.metricbeat 360, elastic_agent 12, filebeat 6, syslog 6, and C-21d with 528/360/14/6/4. Suppression is therefore earned twice: the story stops the Elastic Agent on dev-ws-1, and the live baselines show this envelope routinely carried hundreds of events per hour that are now entirely absent. The projection emits exactly the `<suppressed: ...>` marker with a placeholder for the unstated stop time, matching the measurement's `suppressed` delta_kind. The dead C-7d window (window_live false) is correctly not the basis for the reading, since the two live controls independently establish the non-empty baseline.
rows.evidence: The single query (elastic.syslog-ip-search) over the operation window 2026-07-25T09:35–09:45Z returns row_count 0 with no values, despite the columns (events, data_stream.dataset) being present. Two live controls return a populated baseline for the same host.name == "dev-ws-1": C-14d (window_live: true) has 5 rows — system.auth 444, elastic_agent.metricbeat 360, elastic_agent 12, elastic_agent.filebeat 6, system.syslog 6 — and C-21d (window_live: true) has 5 rows — system.auth 528, metricbeat 360, elastic_agent 14, system.syslog 6, filebeat 4. Even prorating the 60-minute controls to the 10-minute observed window (~74 auth and ~60 metricbeat events expected), the observed count of zero across every dataset means the host stopped emitting entirely; the distinction is carried by the events count per data_stream.dataset. The empty C-7d control is disregarded because window_live is false, but the two live controls are sufficient to establish a non-empty baseline.

rows.evidence:
The single query (elastic.sshd-auth-history, web-1, 09:35–09:45Z) returned row_count: 0 with the
aggregation columns accepted/failed/source.ip/user.name and an empty values list. Its three controls
do not agree: C-7d (2026-07-18) has window_live: false and a null payload, so it measures nothing;
C-14d (2026-07-11, live) returns 2 rows (svc.config-mgmt 6 accepted/0 failed; svc.reports 0
accepted/72 failed); C-21d (2026-07-04, live) returns row_count: 0 with empty values. With one live
control non-empty and the other live control empty — and both controls widened to 60 minutes against
a 10-minute observation window — the payloads do not establish whether zero sshd auth rows on web-1
is routine (absent) or a dark stream (suppressed). A live, duration-comparable control on web-1 that
consistently returned non-zero accepted/failed rows would have settled it.

rows.rationale:
The lead's only query, `cmdb.host-trust-edges` with `{host: dev-ws-1}`, returned a payload carrying just `_note: "state lookup; not an event stream"` and the echoed params — no rows, no timestamped fields — and the baseline is `[]` because a CMDB lookup has no `@timestamp` bounds to shift.
Per `state_and_lookup_systems`, that is `state-only` by construction, not an unmeasured or dead window, which matches the measurement of record.
With no event stream and no control to diff against, there is no delta for the projection to represent, so the empty projection asserts nothing false and omits nothing the telemetry carries.
Notably it also declines to invent CMDB content (role, criticality, owner, trust edges) that the story never states, which would have been the fabrication risk here.
rows.evidence: The lead has a single query, `cmdb.host-trust-edges` with params `{host: dev-ws-1}`, and its observed payload carries only `_note: "state lookup; not an event stream"` plus the echoed params — no event rows, no timestamped columns. The baseline is an empty list because a CMDB lookup carries no `@timestamp` bounds to shift, so no control window exists by construction. Per `state_and_lookup_systems`, cmdb queries return an entity record rather than an event stream and have no baseline-diff semantics. This is `state-only`, not a missing or dead-window measurement, and with only one decidable query there is no cross-query disagreement to record.
